title: Mistral Retail — account conviction & outbound play map
content:
Goal: fast test of a Retail Ops pilot with Mistral (regional chain, ~120 stores). Objective is to validate 1) latency & cost constraints for on-prem inference use-case; 2) integrated receipts/returns assistant that reduces CS handle time by 30%; 3) willingness to sign a 12–18 month Dedicated commitment if ROI is proven.

Quick contextual notes (raw):
- Company: Mistral Retail (founded 2012), midwest-focused, omnichannel with heavy POS customization.
- Why them: tech-savvy merchandising team, big seasonal peaks, already using a cloud-based recommendation engine (vendor: BreezeRec).
- Potential stakeholders: Head of Retail Ops (Emily Ramos), Dir. of Engineering (Ethan Park), Head of CX (Marcus Holt), Procurement (Sourcing: Linda Wu).
- Red flags: procurement insists on SOC2 + data residency language; they prefer single-tenant solutions for PII; current infra includes a small colo footprint in Chicago — candidate for Redwood Private.

Hypotheses (what we want to prove in a pilot):
1) Real-time receipts parsing and suggested-resolution flow can cut CS avg handle time from 6:20 to <=4:30 for returns.
2) Using Dedicated instances with prefix caching, we can keep p95 token latency < 220ms for a 1024-token window during BFCM-like traffic patterns.
3) Model quality yields >90% first-pass resolution suggestions (measured vs human decisions on a 500-sample label set).

Value props to emphasize in outreach (short):
- Predictable latency at scale (Dedicated + canary fallback to open models).
- Deterministic unit economics: batching + caching guidance to cut per-ticket cost by ~40%.
- Private option for PII/PCI workflows with KMS/HSM integrations.

Cold sequence sketch (multi-channel, 3 touch + personal follow):
1) Email 1 (subject: "Reducing return-handling time at Mistral — quick idea") — 1 paragraph, results-led, cite our Dedicated case study (small retailer reduced CS load 28%). CTA: 15-min exploratory call.
2) LinkedIn note — short mention of email + offer to share a one-pager about on-prem pilot.
3) Email 2 (4 days) — a short sample workflow: show step-by-step of receipt -> parsed -> suggested resolution -> agent confirmation. Include prox cost estimate.
4) Phone (voicemail) — reference email + one metric to pique interest.
5) Follow-up from Solutions (if reply): 30-min tech sync request, propose runway for a 6-week pilot.

Elevator pitch (for SDR -> AE handoff):
"We help retailers cut manual returns and CS time by running LLM-powered assistants where your data stays in your network. Predictable latency, clear per-ticket economics, and a playbook for rolling from pilot to Dedicated capacity."

Objection handling cheat-sheet (quick bullets):
- "We can't put PII in the cloud": Redwood Private + KMS + SOC2 + optional on-prem bundle.
- "LLMs are too expensive": show Optimize recommendations (quantization + prefix caching) and sample cost model for 120 stores.
- "Latency during peaks": describe autoscaling, canary fallback to lighter model variants, and trace-based SLOs in Redwood Console.
- "How do you measure accuracy?": we propose a 500-sample label set and automatic regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

Pilot plan (6 weeks) — proposed sprint-level milestones:
Week 0: Contract basics + security questionnaire kickoff.
Week 1: Ingest sample receipts + baseline CS metrics.
Week 2–3: Model selection + prompt engineering + integrate prefix cache.
Week 4: Shadow run (agents see suggestions, no autopicks).
Week 5: A/B test (agents using suggestions vs control) + collect metrics.
Week 6: Final analysis, ROI deck, decision: extend to Dedicated or Private.

Success metrics (candidate KPIs):
- CS avg handle time (% delta)
- First-contact resolution rate
- Suggested-action adoption rate by agents
- Per-ticket inference cost
- P95 latency during stress windows

Data & engineering notes (for tech sync):
- Ingest formats: JSON receipts API + SFTP historical dump (CSV).
- Expected avg tokens per request: 400–800 with structured metadata.
- Preferred integration: webhook + REST inference calls, optional gRPC for Dedicated.
- Compliance: need to confirm PCI-scope boundaries; likely mask CC digits before any external transit.

Open Qs / action items (me as owner):
- [ ] Confirm point of contact for procurement (ask Emily for procurement lead).
- [ ] Get anonymized sample of 1k receipt texts from Mistral for accuracy estimate.
- [ ] Prep short dedicated-cost estimate for 3 capacity tiers. Priya to draft.
- [ ] Spin up a quick demo script that shows latency under simulated peak (Liam helping with load).
- [ ] Draft a 1-page security summary (for Linda Wu).

Intro email draft (raw):
Subject: Quick idea to shave minutes off return handling at Mistral
Hi Emily —
I know you're busy so I'll be short: we help retailers run LLM-driven return-assistants inside customer-controlled environments (so PII stays in your network) and reliably reduce CS handling time. We've run pilots with similar mid-market retailers and seen ~25–35% lower handle time during peak windows.
Would you be open to 15 minutes next week to explore whether this maps to Mistral's return flows? I can share a short ROI sketch.
Best,
Jordan Reyes

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep the ask low initially — focus on operations win not full platform sale.
- Emphasize rollback and canary options early to ease SRE concerns.
- If procurement pushes back on timeline, offer a security deep-dive with our compliance lead as next step.
- Attachments: include anonymized case study + quick cost table.

End.
